questions.q: Let $f(x)$ be a real differentiable function such that $f(0)=1$ and $f(x+y)=f(x) f^{\prime}(y)+f^{\prime}(x) f(y)$ for all $x, y \in \mathbf{R}$. Then $\sum_{\mathrm{n}=1}^{100} \log _{\mathrm{e}} f(\mathrm{n})$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\because f(x+y)=f(x) \cdot f(y)+f(x) \cdot f(y), \forall x, y \in R$ ....(i)
And $f(0)=1$  ....(ii)
Now replace $x$ by zero and $y$ by zero we get
$\begin{aligned}
& f(0)=f(0) f(0)+f(0) f(0) \\
& 1=f(0)+f(0) \\
& \therefore \quad f^{\prime}(0)=\frac{1}{2} ...(iii)
\end{aligned}$
Now replace $y$ by zero in equation (i), we get
$f(x)=\frac{1}{2} f(x)+f^{\prime}(x)$
or, $\frac{1}{2} f(x)=f^{\prime}(x)$
then $\frac{f^{\prime}(x)}{f(x)}=\frac{1}{2}$
hence $\ln |f(x)|=\frac{x}{2}+c$
Put $x=0$, we get $c=0\therefore \quad \ln |f(x)|=\frac{x}{2}$
Then $\sum_{n=1}^{100} \ln (f(\eta))=\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{2}{2}+\frac{3}{2}+\ldots+\frac{100}{2}\right)=\frac{5050}{2}=2525$
